title: runtime-anomaly-hypothesis-and-investigation-patterns
author: Elena Kim
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes a reproducible, hypothesis-driven approach to investigating anomalies in the inference serving runtime. It connects high-level symptom detection (SLO breaches, alerts) to concrete telemetry signals, framed hypotheses, experiments to validate/invalidated each hypothesis, and actionable mitigations. The goal is to reduce time-to-root-cause and to produce repeatable remediation recipes for production incidents and slow regressions.

Scope and intent:
- Scope: inference serving runtime (components including runtime-dispatcher, kernel-manager, batch-aggregator, kv-cache-proxy, model-loader).
- Not in scope: control-plane authentication workflows, billing ingestion pipelines.
- Intended audience: oncall SREs, runtime engineers, profiling/benchmarking leads.

Quick triage signals (first 5 minutes):
1) Alert: p95 generation latency > 2x baseline over 10 minutes.
2) Increase in kernel.exec.ns or kernel.queue_depth metric with correlated GPU saturation.
3) Drop in kvcache.hit_rate with a rise in model-load ops.
4) Elevated rpc.retries or grpc.stream_errors from clients.

Important SLO thresholds (examples):
- p50 token latency: 25ms (baseline)
- p95 token latency: 120ms (SLO)
- Error rate: <0.5%
- GPU utilization: target 60–85% for steady-state, sustained >95% requires investigation

Telemetry mapping table (frequently useful signals):
- dispatch.queue_length: backlog indicating dispatch bottleneck
- kernel.exec.ns: total kernel runtime per request
- kernel.wait.ns: blocking/wait time (memory or scheduling)
- gpu.utilization.percent: device saturation metric
- kvcache.hits / kvcache.requests: cache effectiveness
- model.loader.latency: model swap/load times
- rpc.latency.ms / rpc.errors: client-visible RPC health

Hypothesis-driven investigation workflow (ordered, repeatable):
1) Gather context (0–3 minutes)
   - Which routes/models are affected? Check per-route dashboards and token-level breakdowns.
   - Is the issue global or tenant-scoped? Filter traces by tenant_id.
   - Has a rollout or kernel change occurred recently? Check deployment activity and recent release notes.
2) Rapid signal correlation (3–8 minutes)
   - Pull time-series for dispatch.queue_length, kernel.exec.ns, gpu.utilization.percent, kvcache.hit_rate for the last 30m.
   - Use trace search to find representative slow traces and annotate: where time is spent (dispatch, kernel, GPU, I/O).
3) Form 2–3 concrete hypotheses (8–12 minutes)
   - Example hypotheses: (A) Kernel scheduling contention due to a new priority plugin; (B) KV cache thrash caused by eviction policy change; (C) Model swap storm increasing model.loader.latency.
4) Design minimal experiments (12–25 minutes)
   - Reduce experiment blast radius. Example experiments: pin traffic to model-variant-stable for 10 minutes; temporarily revert priority plugin; increase cache capacity on a single shard; scale out one node pool.
   - For each experiment list expected metric deltas and acceptance criteria.
5) Execute and observe (25–45 minutes)
   - Run a single experiment, capture pre/post snapshots, and do not conflate multiple changes.
   - If an experiment changes consumer-visible latency in the expected direction with statistical significance (p < 0.05 on 5m windows), mark hypothesis supported.
6) Remediate and validate (45–90 minutes)
   - Implement mitigation with a rollback plan and run a controlled canary.
   - Run synthetic traffic from the benchmarking suite to validate throughput and latency under representative shapes.
7) Postmortem and long-term action (>90 minutes)
   - Document root cause, corrective actions, and add automated alerts or regressions tests to the benchmarking harness.

Hypothesis templates (copyable):
- Symptom: "p95 latency +X%, kernel.exec.ns increased by Y%"
- Hypothesis: "Priority plugin P increased kernel preemption causing context-switch overhead leading to higher kernel.wait.ns"
- Prediction: "If we disable plugin P on a canary, kernel.wait.ns should decrease by >= 30% and p95 should return to baseline"
- Experiment: "Disable plugin P for tenant T for 10 min"
- Acceptance: "p95 reduction observed and no increase in error rate"

Common commands and snippets (use internal tooling):
- Fetch recent traces: curl -s "https://tracing.internal/api/search?service=runtime-dispatcher&from=-30m" | jq .
- Snapshot metrics: rd-metrics query 'avg(kernel.exec.ns){service:runtime-dispatcher}[30m]' --output csv
- Run a short profiler capture: rd-profiler sample --target runtime-dispatcher --duration 120s --sample-rate 500 --output /tmp/profile-$(date +%s).pb
- Replay synthetic load (local harness): ./bench/simulate_workload.sh --shape short-burst --qps 200 --duration 300

Profiling configuration recommendations (table):
- profiler.sampling_rate: 250–2000 (per-second samples) depending on traffic
- trace.sampling_pct: 0.1% for global, 5% for canary tenants
- kernel.telemetry.level: normal | verbose (use verbose only for targeted experiments)

YAML example: (use in experiment manifests)
profile_experiment:
  target: runtime-dispatcher
  duration_seconds: 120
  sampling_rate: 1000
  collect_gpu_counters: true

Benchmark reproduction recipe (short-burst tail latency spike):
1) Identify representative request template from traces (use top 5 slow traces).
2) Use bench/simulate_workload.sh with --seed from production trace and --preserve-headers to reproduce routing.
3) While running, capture profiler and kernel telemetry: rd-profiler sample + rd-metrics snapshot.
4) Compare traces to baseline and inspect kernel.exec/ns distribution per request stage.

Common root causes and remediation matrix:
- Cause: kernel preemption/priority inversion -> Mitigation: revert priority plugin, apply cooperative-preemption patch, add fairness token accounting; longer term: scheduler autotune.
- Cause: kvcache thrash after cache-ttl tuning -> Mitigation: increase cache shard capacity, roll back TTL change, add eviction-guard thresholds.
- Cause: model loader storm -> Mitigation: increase model-loading concurrency limits, rate-limit admin rollouts, implement staggered warmstart.

Decision criteria for rollback vs mitigation:
- Rollback immediately if error rate >1% AND p95 > 2x baseline after change.
- Mitigate (config change) if CPU/GPU metrics indicate resource pressure but error rates are stable.

Telemetry signal ownership and useful dashboards:
- runtime-dispatcher SRE dashboard: service p95/p99, dispatch.queue_length, rpc.errors. Owner: runtime-sre.
- kernel-manager dashboard: kernel.exec.ns heatmap, kernel.queue_depth, kernel.wait.ns. Owner: runtime-kernel-team.
- kv-cache dashboard: hit_rate, eviction_rate, load_latency. Owner: infra-cache-team.

Escalation and communication template:
1) Pager duty -> page oncall for runtime-dispatcher.
2) Create incident channel and post initial hypothesis, supporting signals, and planned experiment.
3) Update every 15 minutes until mitigated.
4) After incident close, attach profiler capture and experiment notes to the postmortem.

Runbook snippets (ready-to-run):
- Quick revert of recent kernel plugin:
  1. Check rollout id: rd-deploy list --service kernel-manager --last 4
  2. rd-deploy rollback --service kernel-manager --id <rollout-id> --canary 10%
  3. Monitor kernel.exec.ns, kernel.wait.ns, and p95 for 15 minutes

- Emergency kvcache scale (single shard):
  1. rd-cache scale --shard=shard-5 --replicas=2
  2. rd-cache set --shard=shard-5 --max-entries=2000000
  3. Observe eviction_rate drop and kvcache.hit_rate increase in 5m window

Post-incident hygiene checklist:
- Add a targeted regression test to the benchmarking suite (include the request template and seed).
- Create an alert tuned to the specific leading metric that surfaced the root cause (e.g., kernel.queue_depth > 80 percentile for 10m).
- Schedule a follow-up to discuss longer-term fixes in the runtime architecture weekly.

- Scheduler autotune playbook: /eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/slo-driven-scheduler-autotune-playbook-2026
- Benchmarking harness docs: /eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/microbenchmark-suite-variance-analysis-2025

Appendix: Example incident timeline (realistic condensed):
- 09:05 Alert fired: p95 spike on region-us-east-1
- 09:08 Quick triage: dispatch.queue_length up 3x, kernel.exec.ns up 40%
- 09:15 Hypothesis formed: new priority plugin rollout increased preemption overhead
- 09:20 Revert plugin on canary -> p95 drops 45% in 12 minutes
- 09:35 Full rollback and canary verification -> incident mitigated
- 10:30 Postmortem assigned and regression test added to suite

Ownership and contacts:
- Runtime SRE lead: Marcus Li (pager duty)
- Kernel team primary: Priya Shah
- Benchmarks owner: Daniel Ortega

Notes and caveats:
- This playbook emphasizes small, measurable experiments. Avoid making multiple concurrent changes during an investigation.
- When profiling GPU kernels, expect additional overhead—use sampling windows no longer than 2–5 minutes for production canaries.

If you have questions or want to add a new hypothesis template, ping the runtime-team channel on Slack and attach any relevant traces or profiler outputs.
